claim: The demo study asks whether spaced retrieval beats massed rehearsal for durable vocabulary retention.
Participants were randomized into spaced versus massed conditions, and the spaced arm reviewed words at expanding intervals across four weeks.

evidence.quote: The spaced group reviewed each target word at expanding intervals over four weeks

claim: On the delayed test, recall was 68 percent for the spaced group versus 41 percent for the massed group (synthetic fixture numbers).
Match retrieval cues between training and test deliberately: cue overlap can inflate the measured benefit, so it must be reported.
These figures are synthetic fixtures and must never be cited as empirical findings; provenance has to travel with the note.
The control group achieved near-perfect scores on every test.

evidence.quote: the control group scored 99 percent on every test
